text:
oncall-bot: ALERT: high 5xx rate detected on /v1/generate (hosted). Threshold breached: 6.2% over 1m. Paging eng-oncall primary. Link: https://ops.redwood.example/incidents/INC-1234 :rotating_light:

kevin: grabbing this — I'm on the tail end of my shift but will be primary for the first 10m. handoff to @maria in 10. ETA 10m.

maria: noted. I'll take primary after 10m — can you paste quick triage so I know what to look at? any customer-facing impact yet?

kevin: quick summary: sudden spike in 5xx for hosted inference across multiple model routes, started ~1729456700. Error looks like downstream grpc timeouts from runtime nodes -> 504 surface. No obvious config change. Affected customers: 3 medium accounts, one large customer seeing degraded latency.

kevin: immediate checks I ran: 
```
# check runtime pool health
curl -s https://runtime-pool.internal/health | jq .
# tail error logs for the last 5m
kubectl logs -l app=redwood-runtime --tail=200 | grep "grpc" | tail -n 50
# query autoscaler metrics
kubectl get hpa -n runtime
```

jess: FYI do we know if this is runtime-specific or infra (network/instances)? I'm triaging from infra side. Seeing some elevated socket errors on host nodes 10.2.x.x.

runtime-oncall: from runtime side we see increased KV cache misses and some timeouts to the tokenizer service — coincident with the 5xx spike. Stack traces show "context deadline exceeded" from tokenizer grpc.

infra-oncall: confirmed host kernel logs show transient NIC errors around 1729456725 on a subset of nodes. Could be a noisy NIC or driver bug. I'm spinning up replacement nodes and cordoning suspect ones.

security-oncall: quick question — any signs of unusual egress or suspicious access? If it's a noisy customer/network scan we may need to escalate. I don't see obvious auth anomalies yet.

support-lead: customer-impact note: the large customer (acme-corp) is seeing ~40% request failures; they just DM'd customer success asking for ETA. Recommend we prepare a short blurb.

kevin: mitigation path I'm trying now: 1) temporarily route affected traffic to a fallback model variant (lighter model) 2) spin up extra runtime pods in healthy AZs 3) cordon/replace suspect infra nodes. If fallback looks good, that buys time.

maria: copying runbook steps from runbooks/inference-5xx: https://wiki.redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-5xx
Runbook quick snippet: 
```
1. Identify common failure signature (504 vs 500 vs 429)
2. Check runtime and tokenizer service tails
3. If tokenizer timeouts, route traffic to tokenizer pool B
4. If infra NIC errors, cordon host and migrate pods
5. Consider model-variant fallback: route to model: gpt-medium instead of gpt-large
```

maria: I'll take primary now. kevin, pls stay as secondary for 20m overlap. I'll open the incident page and post status. jess/infra-oncall/runtime-oncall, coordinate whether this is runtime or infra mitigation — we may need an owner from both teams on the incident.

jess: I'll own infra-side replacements and NIC investigation. setting an action: replace 3 hosts, confirm kernel/drivers.

runtime-oncall: I'll own runtime mitigations: shift traffic to tokenizer pool B and watch KV cache latencies.

security-oncall: I'll monitor for suspicious access and will stand by. No immediate escalation unless we see auth/evidence.

support-lead: I'll draft a customer-facing status: "We're investigating increased errors on hosted inference. Our engineers are working on a mitigation and we'll post updates every 15 minutes." Need approval from incident owner before sending.

maria: approved. post the blurb to the affected account channels and send to CSM.

kevin: opened incident: INC-1234 https://ops.redwood.example/incidents/INC-1234 — added initial summary and RCA placeholder.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-1234 created by kevin. Paging hooks: runtime-oncall, infra-oncall, security-oncall, support-lead. Priority: P2.

maria: cross-team routing question: if tokenizer service is root cause, is that runtime responsibility or infra? For quick decisions: runtime handles service-level fixes (cache / pool routing / graceful degradation). Infra handles host-level (NIC, kernel, instance replacements). Security only if it's an auth/exfil issue. Support handles customer comms.

jess: agree with that split. We'll maintain a single incident channel and tag requests with 'runtime:' or 'infra:' prefix for task assignment to avoid confusion.

maria: also note a coverage gap next shift: europe primary will be unassigned between 0300-0400 UTC tomorrow (no volunteers). tagging rotation leads to fill that window. @kevin can you flag on the schedule?

kevin: noted. I'll ping rotations channel and try to get a volunteer. If no one picks up, escalate to eng-manager for coverage.

support-lead: for customer escalation path: if >30% failure for >15m we trigger account executive outreach. Current is 40% for one customer for ~7m, so keep close.

runtime-oncall: mitigation status update (1729457000): routed affected routes to tokenizer pool B; error rate dropped to 2.1% and latency improved. Continuing validation.

infra-oncall: replaced two suspect hosts and cordoned the third (1729457055). NIC errors not observed on new hosts. Monitoring.

maria: good. keep monitoring for 30m. kevin, if everything stable at that time you can complete handoff to next primary.

kevin: acknowledged. I'll stay on overlap and then handoff when stable.

security-oncall: no auth/egress anomalies so far. marking security watch as cleared for now but will reopen if anything shows up.

support-lead: customer blurb posted and CSM notified.

maria: closing note: incident remains open while we monitor; tentative next step is to schedule a post-incident RCA with runtime+infra+support. Action items added to INC-1234. Thanks everyone. :v:
